title: The Battle of Lepanto, 1571 — and the wounded soldier who wrote Don Quixote
sources: Wikipedia: Battle of Lepanto — 7 October 1571, the Holy League (Spain, Venice and allies, arranged by Pope Pius V) against the Ottoman fleet in the Gulf of Patras; the largest naval battle in Western history since classical antiquity, more than 450 warships; the last major engagement in the Western world fought almost entirely between rowing vessels; an 'infantry battle on floating platforms'; John of Austria commanded; Ali Pasha's galley drove into the Real; Ali Pasha was killed; the Christians captured 117 galleys and sank or destroyed some 83; many thousands of Christian slaves were rescued; it is said janissaries ran out of weapons and threw oranges and lemons; the Ottomans rebuilt their fleet within about six months

Wikipedia: Miguel de Cervantes — sailed on the Marquesa; although suffering from malaria he was given command of a skiff; received three wounds, two in the chest and one that rendered his left arm useless; called 'El manco de Lepanto'; captured by Barbary pirates in 1575, five years in captivity; Don Quixote, Part One published 1605; no authenticated portrait exists — the one most often associated with him is attributed to Juan de Jáuregui

Also on this day (candidates.md / Wikipedia On This Day): 1849 Edgar Allan Poe died under mysterious circumstances; 1916 Georgia Tech beat Cumberland 222–0; 1959 Luna 3 transmitted the first photographs of the far side of the Moon

Images (public domain, Wikimedia Commons): Battle of Lepanto, unidentified painter, late 16th c.; Andrea Vicentino (1603, detail); Cornelis de Wael; Martin Rota engraving (1572); Ignazio Danti fresco map; Sánchez Coello, John of Austria (1567); Venetian galleass drawing; Don Quixote first edition title page (1605); portrait attributed to Jáuregui; Poe daguerreotype (1849); Luna 3 far side (1959)

post.facebook:
On this day in 1571, the Battle of Lepanto was fought off the coast of Greece.

The Holy League — Spain, Venice and their allies — met the Ottoman fleet in the largest naval battle in the West since antiquity: more than 450 warships, most of them rowed by hand. The flagships crashed together and soldiers fought hand to hand. The Ottoman admiral was killed and the League captured 117 galleys. It is said that some janissaries, out of weapons, threw oranges and lemons.

On the galley Marquesa, a young Spanish soldier sick with malaria fought anyway. He was wounded twice in the chest, and a third wound left his left arm useless for life. He became known as "the one-handed man of Lepanto". His name was Miguel de Cervantes — and 34 years later he published Don Quixote.

Also on 7 October: Edgar Allan Poe died in 1849 in circumstances still unexplained, and in 1959 Luna 3 sent back the first photographs of the far side of the Moon.
